settings.title: Why AI without governance becomes a business risk

settings.css_classes: f3-aia-stack f3-aia-stack--20 f3-aia-why__aside f3-rv f3m-3ce4813 f3g-2cf5431

settings.editor: AI adoption moves quickly. Governance has to keep up.
Employees and teams adopt new AI tools faster than formal governance can adapt.
Without defined accountability, AI-related security, operational and business risks are hard to manage.
Employees need practical guidance on approved tools, acceptable use, data handling and prohibited activities.
AI applications and use cases need security expectations that match your organization’s risk level.
As AI applications and use cases multiply, governance needs to grow alongside them.

settings.title: Set the rules before AI spreads, not after

settings.editor: AI governance shouldn’t start only after AI is embedded across the organization. Setting governance early lets security, technology and business teams know their responsibilities before adoption becomes hard to manage.
Define policies, responsibilities, acceptable-use requirements and security expectations.
Review new tools and use cases against your governance requirements.
Update governance as new applications, users, integrations and risks appear.
Keep policies, responsibilities and security requirements aligned with how AI use is changing.
